h3_prompt:
Subject: Vertical 9:16, one continuous 11-second single-character narrative. Show exactly one physical instance of the established mouse-ear mutant girl from the bound character references. Preserve her small body, slender limbs, white short hair with eye-covering fringe and top curl, large translucent pale-purple mutated mouse-ear structures attached at both sides of the head, quiet cautious face, loose pale short tunic, dark collar, cuffs, hem and shorts, dark cross-body strap, existing side bag, pale socks and oversized dark shoes. Picture 1 and the secondary identity view represent the same single person, never multiple people.

Movement: From 0 to 2 seconds she stands quietly with both feet planted, shoulders slightly gathered and both hands near her body. From 2 to 4 seconds one faint nonverbal dry tap or air resonance occurs off screen from one side; the source is never shown. From 4 to 6 seconds only the nearer translucent ear pivots a few degrees toward the sound, followed by a smaller settling movement from the other ear; her torso and feet remain still. From 6 to 8 seconds her eyes follow the ear direction and her head turns only a few degrees, without stepping. From 8 to 10 seconds one hand gently presses the already existing side bag against her hip, tightening her compact posture without changing the strap layout. From 10 to 11 seconds all movement stops; her attention remains oriented toward the sound while her original position and cautious distance are preserved.

Scene: Picture 2 defines SCENE-08, the same two-color strange-village environment, its existing spatial continuity, negative space and original palette logic. Use only village forms, ground, depth layers and color relationships visibly supported by the bound scene image. Do not invent a door, bridge, rope, stall, animal, creature, person, machine, sign or story prop. The off-screen sound remains nonvisual and does not create a second subject.

Camera: One locked eye-level three-quarter knee-up medium shot for the entire sequence. Keep both mutated ears, face, torso, cross-body strap and side bag readable in one stable composition, with enough empty space above and beside the ear movement. Fixed framing, fixed focal length, no push-in, no pull-back, no pan, no tilt, no tracking, no cut, no transition and no split-screen composition.

Lighting: Preserve the bound character materials and the scene reference's original two-color palette logic. Use one fixed soft diffuse light throughout. Keep the pale-purple ear translucency restrained and consistent; no flashing, relighting, weather change, sudden saturation shift or color redesign.

Atmosphere: Quiet, cautious and attentive rather than frightened or theatrical. Use clear two-dimensional hand-drawn shapes, clean variable-width ink contours, light watercolor softness, low-saturation shadows and sufficient negative space only where compatible with the bound character and scene references. Do not copy another character's cyan-white energy body, materials or identity.

Audio: Ambient soundscape: very light village air, faint distant structural creak and soft cloth movement, with one small nonverbal dry tap or air resonance at 2 to 4 seconds. Emotional sound cue: one restrained thin suspended tone enters after the ear turns and fades into the final stillness, with no lyrics and no strong beat. Audio supports spatial direction, ear-first action readability and cautious emotion; it does not drive cuts and is not music-video editing.

Negative: exactly one character and one physical body, no duplicate character, no second human figure, no split screen, no clone or mirror-double, no mirror duplicate, no reflection person, no crowd, no NPC, no visible sound source, no rabbit ears, no tail, no horns, no wings, no armor, no weapon, no invented prop, no extra limbs, no deformed hands, no altered strap layout, no missing side bag, no camera movement, no cut, no transition, no weather change, no abrupt color shift, no text overlay, no watermark, no abrupt redesign.
